newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen slightly firmer ahead of key data.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen slightly firmer ahead of key data.

text.p: Key March three-month euroyen interest rate futures were slightly firmer by Friday midday with many operators sidelined ahead of widely watched May industrial output data due at 1.30 p.m. (0430 GMT).
"The market is waiting to see if the industrial output data confirms Wednesday's stronger-than-expected results of BOJ's tankan," said a city bank dealer.
A speech by Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita starting at 0040 p.m. (0340 GMT) is also awaited, traders said.
The March ended the morning up 0.01 at 98.77 on the back of firmness in yen bonds. Turnover was a small 14,218 contracts.
It moved between 98.75 and 98.79 after opening at 98.76.
Economists polled by Reuters forecast increases in May industrial output ranging from 1.2 to three percent, compared with a revised month-on-month drop of 0.5 percent in April.
If the May figure is stronger than expected, the contract may fall toward 98.60, breaking through technical support at around 98.67, a second city bank dealer said.

If the data is weaker than expected, it could rise as high as 98.88, regaining half of the ground it lost during a sharp fall from 98.98 to 98.72 on Wednesday triggered by the stronger-than-expected tankan, he said.

In the interbank market, the key overnight call rate fell to around 0.50 percent from Thursday's 0.52 due to the BOJ's more accommodative operation this morning. It was the first time since June 11 that the BOJ conducted an operation leaving a surplus of some 300 billion yen in the market.

Traders said the BOJ operation was aimed at easing recent upward pressure in long-term funds with maturities of two weeks or longer. The offer rate of the key three-month certificates of deposit (CD) rose to 0.66 percent this morning from Thursday's 0.64 percent partly because the CDs to be issued on and after Friday will mature after the interim fiscal year-end.
